Anyway, my world did collapse the day they left. It collapsed like towering buildings, once stately and sturdy, falling suddenly as if they’re knees had gone out from under them. The buildings did not go down calmly, smoothly, or quietly, but sharply causing debris to fall and to float through the air. Those buildings were my life. My sturdy existence. Overnight my everything changed. And it didn’t just happen to me.

That morning was predictable in its chaos.

But Clara liked schedules almost as much as her morning cup of orange pomegranate juice. She had a cup in her hand as I ran down the stairs to meet her. Clara Davis was dressed for work. She had on an orange button-up blouse that was sure to make even the most self-assured, vibrant traffic cones envious, paired with faded blue jeans and tall black leather boots. You know, the kind with the big shiny buckle on the sides. 
Some may say that this is an odd way to dress for work. Clara’s boss would likely agree with those “some”. But Clara knew that her boss Thomas Reed was an unimaginative sort of fellow. Thus his opinions were taken with a whole bucket full of salt in the Davis household. As for me, I adored my mother's eccentricities. Once when I came home from school, I found her crouched on the kitchen table, barefoot. I was eight years old at the time, but still remembered her smiling as I walked through the door. 
“Ellie dear! I’ve found the most wonderful way to stretch out the back of your heels! You simply must try it!” She exclaimed as she beckoned me over. I still believe that my ankles have never felt better than they did that day. 
At the bottom of the stairs, I made a sharp left turn, making a beeline for the study. “Wren! Good morning Wren!” I called in a singsong voice. Wren flapped her wings excitedly when she saw me. She dove out of open door of her cage and swooped over my head. I giggled as the little hairs by my ears took flight with her. Her brown feathers were in slight disarray as she soared around and around. Hey, what girl doesn’t experience a little bedhead? My heart was warm and soft as Wren landed on my shoulder, nuzzling into my neck with her soft wing. 
“Hello little bird.” I greeted her softly. Her reply came back in small tweets, but I understood her hello just the same. She took off again flying around the room until she hovered by the door. I knew what she wanted.
“I know I know. I wish you could come with me today too! You know how I always feel so much better when you’re with me. But they won’t let you come. They would just send you straight back home, like all the other times remember?”
If Wren had shoulders, they would’ve slouched at this. But as a bird, she just sunk a little lower in the air, resigned to another boring day at home. 
“You could go outside! You know, fly around the town, make some bird friends!” I suggested helpfully. Wren seemed to roll her eyes at that as if I should have known how silly a suggestion that was. And I did. Our animal guides, or guidas as they’re normally called, were highly intelligent. They would never be seen hanging out with the normal animals. 

“Ok. I guess I better go. I’ll see you later!” Wren seemed a little extra sad today as she flew back to her cage, but I tried to keep things positive as I waved and met Mom at the front door.
“Here’s your lunch. Remember that I packed an extra cinnamon bun for Julian. I wish I could see his excitement when you give it to him, but you’ll describe it to me after school, won't you dear?  Or better yet, have him over. He always gets so excited and then he gets sugar all over his face when he eats those buns. I’ll make him a whole pan to himself after I get back from work. You’ll tell him I said hello? Thank you, sweet girl. Now let's get a move on.” Mom opened the door and started leading us down the block toward school. 
Yes, I was almost of legal age and my mom still walked me to school every day. I suppose it would make me sound cool to say that she did it against my will. That I was held captive or bribed or guilt-tripped into these daily walks. The truth is that this was my most treasured time every day. Every morning we walked together and talked about all kinds of things.

*   **Bonding:** Guidas form a unique, lifelong bond with a specific human. This bond is described as a guiding partnership that has existed "for generations."
